title: fix: keep known MCP catalogs from delaying new chats
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A new chat can spend ten seconds rediscovering tools from an MCP server that was already discovered successfully. An unresponsive catalog request blocks the first model request, even when healthy servers have already answered.

## User Impact

New chats, subagents, and Code Mode can immediately use a previously discovered MCP catalog while it refreshes in the background. Later turns receive successful catalog changes. A never-discovered server still uses the existing bounded listing deadline; its existing typed failure is included in the current model turn and remains visible in the tool inventory. Calls to unavailable servers retain the existing tool-error behavior and recovery guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead decision by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), not Peter's.

Keep successful catalogs in the existing bundle-MCP manager, bounded by its existing runtime limit and keyed by server configuration, endpoint, and auth scope. Unchanged config reloads retain these facts; manager disposal clears them. Existing per-server concurrency and listing deadlines stay unchanged. Native capability-bound discovery remains private. No new configuration, persistent cache, or production schema change.

The tradeoff is intentional: a turn may advertise the last successful schema while refresh is pending. That turn's catalog remains stable; refreshed schemas apply to later turns. A ready connection can execute a known tool without waiting for catalog refresh. Catalog recovery moves out of send preparation while existing transport-specific tool-call recovery remains. Production source grows by 54 lines to retain bounded identity-scoped facts and expose existing diagnostics; the runtime module itself shrinks by one line.

Related overlap: #137594. This does not depend on that PR or add its Tool Search diagnostics; it uses the existing catalog diagnostic type.

## Evidence

Real HTTP MCP servers through manager acquisition and materialization, on a synthetic btrfs fixture with a 35 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions, and 62,000 workspace files (1.14 GB). Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, with healthy A/A controls:

| Materialization | Before median | After median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Known catalog, hung list | 10,049.057 ms | 1.940 ms |
| Known catalog, 3-second list | 3,009.913 ms | 1.804 ms |
| First-ever healthy list | 7.169 ms | 7.270 ms |
| Known healthy catalog | 8.368 ms | 1.998 ms |

Foreground CPU for the hung case falls from 147.205 to 8.048 ms; refresh-inclusive CPU is 154.898 versus 130.659 ms. Both arms make one initialize and one list request. Refresh work moves off preparation; it is not eliminated. Five-sample ranges and A/A controls show busy-host jitter; these are not population-tail estimates.

The retained-catalog and model-notice regressions fail on exact parent `2b5f1a88ba81e03d51010065c836f48490ebb498`. Focused runtime, reload, Code Mode, prefix-stability, and prompt-context tests pass (144 tests). MCP App browser test and both real Control UI/standalone conformance cases pass, including refresh overlap and cancellation.

A real isolated Gateway/QA channel with a local synthetic inference server delivered every expected reply. Across ten fresh-session sends after seed, first outbound median falls **10,293 → 252 ms**, final outbound **10,300.5 → 260 ms**. A separate first-ever hung run completed all eleven sends at the existing timeout; all eleven actual provider requests contained the unavailable notice and next step.

Separate sampled-allocation profiles (foreground / refresh-inclusive bytes): hung **14,897,816 / 18,062,632 → 3,083,512 / 17,424,304**; slow **4,705,328 / 4,901,840 → 3,531,696 / 4,714,144**; healthy **4,169,656 / 4,321,720 → 3,034,120 / 3,925,608**. These are diagnostic samples, not allocation tail estimates.

Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed; its new test-array lint finding was fixed and targeted type-aware lint/format passed. All other gates pass except five unrelated unused exports, reproduced on the exact parent. Final exact-head CI run 44864878083 passed (60 successful jobs, zero failures). ClawSweeper revision 3 reports zero findings and zero open items on the final head. Introducing changes: publication transport export from #202654 (`39bcc3cc44447`); approval/session permission exports from #201615 (`2b5f1a88ba81e`); workspace-link exports from #202534 (`eb56951a4ca9e`, subsequently repaired by #202879). These are recorded main regressions, not ignored test noise. No task-caused failure is accepted.


Healthy repeat after our build/browser jobs finished: five further pairs measured median **8.557 → 7.781 ms**, maximum **15.124 → 8.566 ms**, foreground CPU **19.577 → 20.037 ms**, total CPU **20.003 → 20.390 ms**. The original candidate tail outlier and this baseline outlier are both retained; no consistent healthy-path regression was found. A/A controls were 8.022/9.131 ms baseline and 10.777/6.699 ms candidate. Other lanes still shared the host.

Reproduce owner measurements with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/mcp-materialize-measure.ts --workspace <synthetic-workspace> --mode hung` (also `slow`, `healthy`; `--cold` for a new identity; `--profile <dir>` separately). Gateway workload: `scripts/bench-channel-turn.mts --mcp-list-delay-ms=-1 --state-dir <synthetic-state> --workspace-dir <synthetic-workspace> --resources`, with `--mcp-first-ever` for cold timeout notice proof. No production data or access used.


The initial CI run exposed task-caused consumer failures, repaired before landing: prompt fixtures now include bundle-tools state, SSE tests observe asynchronous catalog publication, and disconnected stdio calls preserve their existing immediate typed error. Real configured-server tests now prove ready calls overlap a held refresh and the next request after grant revocation or lineage reassignment is rejected before server I/O. The unchanged post-await authorization-fence test also passes. All 54 tests across the six initially failed CI files, both late prompt-admission cases, and 75 owner tests pass; Codex reviewed the complete staged correction with no actionable P0–P2 findings. These failures were not classified as inherited.

A late native-discovery shard also exposed a real shutdown race: catalog reuse allows policy to retire an excluded stdio server during spawn admission. Graceful close previously aborted that admission, losing the process owner’s cleanup receipt. Graceful close now joins startup ownership; forced shutdown retains cancellation. The real app-server/CLI lifecycle test verifies retained calls and complete child retirement, and a held-startup transport regression covers the boundary. The transport repair adds zero production lines. Final transport/process-cleanup proof: 34 tests pass, one Windows-only test skipped locally. The held-startup regression fails on exact parent and passes with the repair.

Landed via native scripts/pr as `52934fb347d00592b947ada9f4a9bfdd15dbcddf`, from reviewed/CI head `ad7e28b5d06ddb1f9b1ede1beff0bd43eebf8bea`. Initial failed CI run 44861019763 was repaired; final run 44864878083 passed. [ClawSweeper final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202902#issuecomment-7056803667) has zero open items; [numbered response and runtime capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202902#issuecomment-7057098414).
